useCase.name: Return an unused credit to a family who leaves the school
useCase.featureRef: 4.11 Refunding an unused credit on withdrawal

intent.name: fee.refund.raise
intent.summary: Propose returning an unused credit to a household that has left the school, after any outstanding charge is settled from it. One step, and no money moves.

request.text: agle bill mein adjust kar dena
request.gloss: just adjust it against the next bill

routesElsewhere.note: While any child remains enrolled the credit is applied to their bill instead, which is what the household expects (BR-2, E1).

request.gloss: the charge was wrong, credit it

routesElsewhere.note: A credit is created there; this returns one that already exists and cannot be used.
Money leaves through a payment voucher on the ordinary route, and only once the Principal has approved it (BR-5, BR-6).

steps.note: One step, producing a proposal at Awaiting approval. Nothing leaves the school and no voucher exists until the Principal approves it (BR-6).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. A child still enrolled, an outstanding charge, an amount above the credit remaining and a payee who is not the guardian on record are all enforced by the API and arrive as errors.
plan.atomicity: One write: the proposal with its amount, method, payee and reason, together with the audit entry or not at all. No money moves, no voucher is raised and the credit balance is untouched — it is still held against the household and could still be applied if a child re-enrols (A5). The original credit and the charge behind it stay in place; a refund is an additional entry, never a deletion (BR-12).

operations.name: fee.refund.raise
operations.idempotencyKey: family_code + amount, since a household carries one open refund proposal at a time
operations.purpose: Raise a refund proposal against a household's unused credit, after settling any charge still outstanding from it.

parameters.name: family_code

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No household matches, or none holding an unused credit.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the candidates with the guardian, the children and the credit held.

parameters.notes: The household holding the unused credit. Every child must have withdrawn — while any remains enrolled the credit is applied to their bill instead (BR-2, E1).

parameters.name: amount
parameters.notes: Greater than zero and not more than the credit remaining after any outstanding charge is settled from it (BR-3, BR-4, E3). A part refund is permitted and the remainder stays held (BR-8). Exactly the figure the actor states.

parameters.name: method
parameters.notes: How the money leaves. Only where the request states it — the method decides what evidence comes back and when the money actually goes.

parameters.name: payee_name
parameters.notes: The guardian on the household record, and nobody else. A person walking in claiming a refund is not evidence of who paid (BR-7, E4).

parameters.name: bank_details
parameters.notes: Account title and number, where the method is a transfer. Never taken from anywhere but the request.

parameters.name: reason
parameters.notes: 20 to 500 characters. Why the credit could not be used. The actor's own words — money leaving the school is read back later.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

errors.meaning: A child in the household is still enrolled.
errors.note: The message names the child and class. The credit goes to their next bill, which is what the household expects (BR-2).

errors.meaning: A charge is outstanding and exceeds the credit held.
errors.note: The household owes the school, not the other way round. The school does not hand back money and chase a debt at the same time (BR-3).

errors.meaning: The amount is more than the credit remaining.
errors.note: There is no route by which a refund creates a debt (BR-4). Never reduce the figure to fit.

errors.meaning: The payee is not the guardian on the household record.
errors.note: A refund is paid to the guardian on the record (BR-7). Correcting the record is UC-03-01, not a step to chain here.

planningRules.rule: Never supply or round the amount. A part refund is permitted (BR-8) and which part is the actor's decision; E3 refusing one above the remaining credit is not a prompt to trim it.
Never name a payee other than the guardian on the household record. A person walking in claiming a refund is not evidence of who paid (BR-7), and money leaving to the wrong hands is not recoverable.
Never raise a refund while a child is still enrolled. E1 is BR-2 working — the credit goes to their next bill, which is what the household expects and what the money is for.

Report the outstanding charges and the credit remaining. Any charge still due is settled from the credit first and only the balance is returned (BR-3) — so the amount refundable is usually less than the credit held, and the actor needs to see both.
Never compose the reason. Money leaving the school is read back later, and BR-6 makes it the Principal's decision on the strength of it.

Never chain the approval or the payment. Accounts raise, the Principal approves and the money leaves through a voucher — three acts, because money leaving the school is not one hand's decision (BR-5, BR-6).
branch_id comes from $session.

reversal.statement: A proposal is approved or returned by the Principal; nothing here withdraws one. No money has moved and the credit is untouched. Where the family re-enrols before it is paid, the credit is simply applied to the new bill instead (A5).

steps.note: One step. It raises the payment voucher through the ordinary route for money leaving the school (BR-5) — no separate refund mechanism exists, so the refund appears in the books like any other payment out.

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. The acting role is enforced by the API and arrives as an error.
plan.atomicity: One write, atomic in itself: the approval, the payment voucher and the audit entry together or not at all. **No money has left yet** — the voucher is raised and the refund waits to be marked paid on the date it actually goes (BR-9). The credit is not yet discharged; that happens when the payment is recorded (BR-10). The original credit and the charge behind it stay in place (BR-12).

planningRules.rule: Never approve a refund in any session but a Principal's or Director's. School Admin approval is not sufficient here — this is money leaving the school (BR-6).

Report that the money has not left yet. Approving raises a voucher; the refund is marked paid separately, on the date it actually goes (BR-9), and a family told the money is on its way when only a voucher exists will ring back.
Never chain the payment onto the approval. The two are separate because the date money leaves and the date it was approved differ whenever a cheque waits for collection (BR-9).
Report that the credit is not yet discharged. It is discharged by exactly what was refunded, when the payment is recorded (BR-10) — until then the household still holds it.

intent.name: fee.refund.pay
intent.summary: Record that an approved refund has actually been paid, on the date the money left. One step, and it discharges the credit.
routesHere: mark the Khan refund paid, the transfer went yesterday

routesHere.text: refund ka paisa de diya hai, mark kar do
routesHere.gloss: the refund money has been handed over, mark it

routesHere: record the refund as paid with the signed acknowledgement

routesElsewhere.note: A refund is marked paid only after it is approved and its voucher raised.

steps.note: One step, and it is the point at which the credit is discharged. The date is when the money actually left, not when it was approved — the two differ whenever a cheque waits for collection (BR-9).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. A refund already marked paid, and a failed ledger posting, are enforced by the API and arrive as errors.
plan.atomicity: One write, atomic in itself: the payment, the discharge of exactly what was refunded, and the audit entry together or not at all (E7). The credit is reduced by exactly the amount refunded, so the household account reads correctly afterwards and cannot be refunded twice (BR-10). Any remainder stays held and can be paid later (BR-8). The original credit and the charge behind it are untouched — a refund is an additional entry, never a deletion (BR-12).

operations.name: fee.refund.pay
operations.idempotencyKey: refund_id, since a refund is paid once and BR-10 depends on it — a repeat must not discharge the credit twice
operations.purpose: Record an approved refund as paid on the date the money left, discharging that much of the household's credit.

errors.meaning: The refund has already been marked paid.
errors.note: The message names the date. A household cannot be refunded twice (BR-10).

errors.written: Nothing. The credit is not discharged.
errors.note: Message: "The refund could not be recorded as paid. The credit is unchanged."

planningRules.rule: Never default the paid date to today. It is when the money actually left, and the two differ whenever a cheque waits for collection (BR-9) — a wrong date misstates when the school's cash went out.
Never mark a refund paid before the money has gone. This discharges the credit (BR-10), and a household whose credit is discharged against a transfer that never left has lost it.
Never re-emit after ALREADY_PAID. A household cannot be refunded twice, and BR-10 is what guarantees it.
Report the remaining credit on a part refund. The remainder stays held and can be paid later (BR-8), and the family should know it is still theirs.
branch_id comes from $session.

reversal.statement: Money that has left cannot be recalled by anything here. Where a refund was paid in error, the household owes the school and that is a fresh charge, not a reversal. The original credit, the charge behind it and the refund all stay in the books (BR-12). The controller must not attempt a compensating call.
